title: Conveyor and Equipment Anomaly Detection from Video
summary: Video and thermal analytics on conveyor transfer points and idler runs that flag belt drift, spillage, chute blockage and hot idlers for maintenance teams to review.

seo.title: Conveyor Anomaly Detection from Video | VipraTech
seo.description: AI that watches conveyor transfer points and idlers on video and thermal cameras, flags belt drift, spillage and hot spots, and drafts work orders.

designed_for: Head of Coal or Material Handling Plant

problem.intro: Long belt conveyors move coal, ore and overburden through crushers, transfer chutes and stockyards, and most faults show visible signs before they become breakdowns. A belt tracking off-centre, spillage building under a chute or an idler running hot is easy to see on camera but hard to catch on a walk-down done once a shift.

pain_points.title: Faults found after the belt is damaged
pain_points.detail: Edge wear, rips and carry-back often come to light only when a belt sway switch trips or a section needs replacement.

pain_points.title: Galleries too long to patrol often
pain_points.detail: Walk-downs cover long galleries and transfer towers, so a developing problem can go unseen between rounds.

pain_points.title: Spillage adds clean-up and fire risk
pain_points.detail: Coal and ore spillage at transfer points means clean-up hours and, for coal, a fire hazard around hot idlers.

pain_points.title: Trips without context
pain_points.detail: Interlock and switch trips show that something happened, not what the belt looked like in the minutes before.

solution.overview: We build a monitoring system for the conveyor sections that matter most: head and tail pulleys, loading points, transfer chutes and idler runs. Fixed cameras, and thermal cameras where heat matters, feed an edge server that learns each view's normal state. Models track the belt edge against its baseline, measure spillage build-up, spot material backing up at chutes and pick out oversized objects on the belt. Thermal frames show idlers and pulleys running hotter than their neighbours. Events are tied to the conveyor's running state, read from the plant historian, and a maintenance engineer reviews each clip before a work order is drafted in your CMMS.
capabilities: Belt edge tracking against a per-view baseline, with drift trends by conveyor
Spillage and pile build-up detection at transfer points and under return idlers
Chute blockage and overloading cues at loading points
Detection of oversized lumps, wood and other foreign objects on the belt surface
Thermal hot-spot detection on idlers and pulleys compared with adjacent rollers
Event clips linked to equipment tags, running state and draft work orders

workflow.title: Choose views and set baselines
workflow.detail: We select camera positions with your maintenance team and record a normal-running baseline for each view.

workflow.title: Read running state
workflow.detail: The system reads conveyor running and load status from the historian in read-only mode, so idle belts do not raise alerts.

workflow.title: Detect anomalies
workflow.detail: Models check each view for drift, spillage, blockage, foreign objects and thermal hot spots.

workflow.title: Score severity
workflow.detail: Events are scored by severity and persistence; low scores are kept as trend data only.

workflow.title: Engineer reviews
workflow.detail: The shift maintenance engineer views the clip and decides whether action is needed now or at the next planned shutdown.

workflow.title: Create the work order
workflow.detail: Confirmed issues become draft notifications or work orders in the CMMS against the right equipment tag.

inputs: Video from conveyor transfer points, loading chutes and galleries
Thermal images from selected idler runs and pulleys
Running and load status tags from the plant historian
Conveyor line list and equipment tags from the CMMS
Past breakdown and belt replacement records
outputs: Anomaly events with clip, equipment tag and severity
Shift list of open events ranked by severity
Draft CMMS notifications or work orders
Belt drift and spillage trends per transfer point
Hot idler list for the next planned shutdown
human_in_the_loop: A maintenance engineer or CHP shift in-charge confirms every event before a work order is raised. The system never stops a conveyor; trips remain with pull-cord switches, belt sway switches and existing interlocks.
integrations: Plant historian such as AVEVA PI or equivalent, read-only
SAP PM, IBM Maximo or another CMMS
Email, Microsoft Teams or WhatsApp alerts to the maintenance team
guardrails: Read-only connection to plant data; no commands to PLC, DCS or drives
Does not replace pull-cord, belt sway or zero-speed switches, or metal detectors
Baselines re-recorded after belt changes or camera moves
Lens obstruction and dust build-up reported as camera faults
Engineer approval before any work order is created
compliance_notes: Plant data access follows zone and conduit boundaries of the kind IEC 62443 describes, agreed with your OT security team.
Supports, and does not replace, the statutory inspection and maintenance records kept for conveyors in mines and plants.

pilot.scope: One critical conveyor line with two or three transfer points and one thermal camera on its most troublesome idler run, alongside normal patrols.
deliverables: Engineer review console linked to equipment tags
Event log compared with patrol and breakdown records

what_we_measure.how: Share of raised events that engineers confirm as real issues.
Time between the first system flag and the issue being found on patrol or by a switch trip, where both occur.
Count of events dismissed as caused by dust, lighting or lens problems.
Engineer time spent per shift reviewing events.

faqs.a: Often some. Existing CCTV can cover spillage and blockage at transfer points, but belt tracking needs a stable view of the belt edge and hot-spot detection needs thermal cameras. We propose placements after a site walk and a look at your current footage.

faqs.q: How do you handle coal dust and poor lighting?
faqs.a: Views are chosen and enclosures specified with dust in mind, and models are tuned on footage from your galleries. The system detects dirty or blocked lenses and raises them as camera faults rather than missing problems silently.

faqs.q: Will this connect to our DCS or PLCs?
faqs.a: Only through a read-only route such as the plant historian, agreed with your OT security team. The system reads running and load status for context and never writes back.

faqs.q: How is this different from vibration monitoring?
faqs.a: It complements it. Vibration and temperature sensors are good at bearing and gearbox faults, while video sees belt tracking, spillage, blockages and objects on the belt. Many plants use both, and our events can sit beside condition monitoring data in the same dashboards.
